content_unit.title: Viewing a flat with Mr Bell

parsed_blocks.text: Anna is new in the city and looks for a home to rent. She reads two advertisements in a shop window. The first is for a small flat with one bedroom. The second is for a studio, just one room with a kitchen in the corner.
The flat is on the ground floor, so Anna does not need to climb any stairs. It is furnished: it already has a bed, a table and some chairs. There is also a small balcony where she can sit outside.

Anna calls the number under the advertisement. A man named Mr Bell answers; he is the landlord of the flat. She asks if the flat is still available. He says yes, and they arrange a viewing for Saturday morning.
On Saturday, Anna meets Mr Bell at the flat. He shows her the bedroom, the kitchen and the balcony. He tells her that the last tenant left the flat very clean.
Anna likes the flat and asks about the rent. Mr Bell says the rent is 450 euros a month. He explains that water and heating are included in this price.
Anna also asks about other bills, like electricity and internet. Mr Bell says the tenant pays these bills every month, apart from the rent.
Before she moves in, Anna pays a deposit. This is extra money that Mr Bell keeps safe until she leaves the flat.
Anna wants to move in soon, so she asks about the date. Mr Bell says she can move in on the first of next month. They agree to sign a contract before then.
A contract is a paper about the flat. It says how much Anna pays and for how long she can stay. Both Anna and Mr Bell sign it together.
The next week, Anna signs the contract in Mr Bell's small office. She is now the tenant of the flat with the sunny balcony.

data.definition: a home with rooms on one floor, usually inside a bigger building; in American English people often say apartment
data.example: The first is for a small flat with one bedroom.

data.definition: a small home with just one main room and a kitchen in the corner; people sometimes call it a studio flat
data.example: The second is for a studio, just one room with a kitchen in the corner.

data.definition: already having furniture like a bed, a table and chairs, so you do not need to buy your own
data.example: It is furnished: it already has a bed, a table and some chairs.

data.definition: the level of a building at the same height as the street, with no stairs to climb; in American English people often call this the first floor
data.example: The flat is on the ground floor, so Anna does not need to climb any stairs.

data.definition: a small platform outside a window or door where you can stand or sit outside
data.example: There is also a small balcony where she can sit outside.

data.definition: the person who owns a flat and rents it to someone else; people also call this person the owner
data.example: He is the landlord of the flat.

data.definition: the person who pays rent and lives in a flat that belongs to someone else; people also call this person the renter
data.example: The last tenant left the flat very clean.

data.definition: a short visit to a flat before you decide to rent it, so you can look around it; people also call this a visit
data.example: They arrange a viewing for Saturday morning.

data.definition: to bring your things to a new home and start living there
data.example: Anna wants to move in soon, so she asks about the date.

data.definition: free for someone to rent, because nobody lives there now
data.example: She asks if the flat is still available.

data.definition: the money that a tenant pays every month to live in a flat
data.example: Mr Bell says the rent is 450 euros a month.

data.definition: money that a tenant pays before moving in, which the landlord keeps safe until the tenant leaves; people also call this a security deposit
data.example: Before she moves in, Anna pays a deposit.

data.definition: money that you pay for things like electricity and internet, apart from the rent; people also call these utilities
data.example: Anna also asks about other bills, like electricity and internet.

data.definition: already part of the price, so you do not pay for it again
data.example: He explains that water and heating are included in this price.

data.definition: a paper that says how much the tenant pays and for how long they can stay, signed by both sides; people also call this a lease or an agreement
data.example: They agree to sign a contract before then.
